## Independent review — Moriarty SP05 financial integration source

I read the manifest and every file in the required scope (paginated, no truncation), performed no execution of any kind, and did not consult other reviewers' output. Hash re-verification was not possible under the permitted tool set, so all SHA-256 values below are recorded as supplied by root, not recomputed by me.

**What the arithmetic actually does.** I re-derived both conservation predicates in `financial-comparison.mjs:136-141` against every stage of `financial-expectations.json`. `ASSET_CONSERVATION` (`out − gross + Δreserve = mint`) and `CONTRACT_RESERVE_CONSERVATION` (`Δreserve = nativeInputs − nativeOutputs`) hold for all eight stages, and they hold *because* the mint-to-self amount is represented once — in `unshieldedInputs` and therefore in Δreserve — rather than being added a second time through `out`. Swap initialize (mint 1 100 000 A = 1 000 000 self + 100 000 to trader; inputs A = 1 000 000; Δreserve = 1 000 000; out = 100 000) is the discriminating case, and it balances only under the corrected representation in `native-effects-refinement.json`. The predicates are also change-robust: wallet-appended payer change enters both `out` and `gross` and cancels, so loan settle balances without expectations knowing the change amount. The refinement is a representation correction, not an economic re-derivation — every kernel field, result record, reserve and net delta is unchanged, consistent with its own `unchanged` list.

**Build boundary.** `proven-assets.mjs:118-173` consumes an externally admitted receipt genuinely: `status:'built'`, `synthetic:false`, `proven:true`, `inspectedProofAssets:true`, and `proofsGenerated===false` are all required together (`:125-129`), the synthetic branch is reachable only via `sourceTestOnly`, the executable loader refuses adapters outright (`:197`), the attempt file must agree on resource/admission/case/outputDir/attempts, and the artifact set is re-fingerprinted before import, inside the module `load` hook, and again after composition. Generated modules are AST-checked for imports, `require`/`eval`/`Function` and dynamic import. There is no path by which a synthetic build yields a `compiledContract`.

**Callable production path.** The chain `loadProvenFinancialContract → loadFinancialContractsSdk → createUnprovenDeployTx → fixed contractAddress → rawTokenType colors → grossByAsset limits → initializeReservations → createProviders` is real and correctly ordered: `integrate-local.mjs:145-152` derives colors from the prepared address before limits are frozen, deletes `grossByLogicalAsset`, and rejects a pre-bound `grossByAsset` (`:125`). `prepare-deployment.mjs` captures `submit`/`call` by reference at prepare time and replays an immutable byte snapshot, which the test at `prepare-deployment.test.mjs:56-67` demonstrates survives adapter mutation. Durability semantics meet the requirement: `active` phase is persisted before every wallet call, submissions/gross/DUST are charged before finalize (`providers.mjs:370-374`), reconstruction refuses on any unresolved `active` or `stopped`, and a crashed lock is never auto-cleared.

Three concrete defects, all small and all in stated-requirement territory:

1. **`receipt.mjs:60` under-verifies payer signatures.** It accepts an input if *any* signature in the offer verifies for that input's owner, and never compares `signatures.length` to `inputs.length`. `providers.mjs:82,90` does this correctly (count equality plus index-aligned `offer.signatures[index]`). Because these transactions have a single payer owning all inputs, an offer carrying one signature for N inputs passes the observer. Impact is bounded (finalized bytes, receipt self-labels `uncertified-I2-observation`), but the observer is the component the requirement designates for "actual UTXO ownership/payer signatures", and the fix is to mirror the existing stricter code.

2. **`financial-comparison.mjs:53-56` imports `compact-runtime` under a version-string check only.** Every other loader in the candidate hash-pins the entry bytes (`integrate-local.mjs:36-42`, `proven-assets.mjs:31-37`). This module derives asset colors (`rawTokenType`) and role capability commitments (`persistentHash`) — the comparator's entire binding layer. In the composed path `loadNativeRuntime` hash-verifies the same `dist/index.js` earlier in the same process, so the integrated risk is low; standalone comparator use (which `compiled-comparison.test.mjs` exercises) is unpinned.

3. **`integrate-local.mjs:157-171` can leak the supplied wallet.** `driverStarted=true` is set before `deps.driver(...)`, and `run-local.mjs:23` throws its `OWNED_PROVIDER_CLEANUP_REQUIRED` guard *outside* its own try/finally. Any throw from the driver before it enters its try leaves `driverResult` undefined, so the `else cleanup=driverResult?.cleanup` branch performs no provider or wallet cleanup at all. Not reachable with the real `createFinancialProviders` return shape, but it defeats the module's own "supplying existing handles transfers cleanup responsibility" contract on a malformed-dependency path.

**Two things a consumer must be told, not defects.** `providers.mjs:422` hardcodes `containmentComplete:false`, so `run-local.mjs:89-93` *always* throws `DRIVER_CLEANUP_INCOMPLETE` and `integrate-local` always throws with `publicIntegrationResult.status:'INCOMPLETE'`. No production configuration can return a resolved success; the outer process must read `INCOMPLETE` plus `financialComparison.status==='PASS'` and own containment itself. Separately, `checkDeadline` takes an exclusive lockfile on every guarded provider call when no operation lock is held; any interleaving with an in-flight `exclusive` section produces a deliberately unrecoverable `reservation lock exists` stop. That is fail-closed by design, but it will terminate a run on ordinary async overlap.

**Negative controls are genuine**, not decorative: 29 comparator mutations covering erased debt, overwritten prior results, third-party payer, gross-replaced-with-net, false `proofVerified`, hidden zero payouts and unknown state fields; provider tests that mutate real WASM transactions to exercise `approvedBalance`, signature presence-without-validity, extra intents and unshielded balancing; a historical-DUST replay over real bytes asserting the unequal `300000000000001` vs `1` fields survive as `encoding:'unresolved'`; and a generated-runtime differential test whose synthetic wallet input is computed by subtracting self-mint claims from `unshieldedInputs` (`compiled-comparison.test.mjs:54-59`) — the exact double-count the refinement addresses. The historical fee finding is correctly absorbed: `receipt.mjs:140-145` retains both values and asserts no relationship, matching the REPORT's recommendation.

The manifest reports `ledger:146, retainedGeneratedRuntime:3`; the launch brief states 150 source tests. I cannot reconcile 149 vs 150 statically and did not run anything.
